key_insight: An invariant neural-network closure recovers key turbulence behavior in coarse-mesh reactor simulations without solving turbulence transport equations.
engineering_relevance: The closure improves molten-salt reactor flow predictions at system-code cost, supporting efficient thermal-hydraulic analysis.
method: Predict elementwise turbulent kinetic energy and timescale from neighboring flow and geometry.
Enforce translation, Galilean, rotation, reflection, and neighbor-order invariance; place non-negative eddy viscosity in the implicit diffusive operator.
Iteratively retrain on SAM flow states against fixed Nek5000 targets to reduce training-to-solver distribution shift.
evidence_signal: In a 120 s pump-coastdown test, velocity error fell from 37.6% to 17.7%, with 12% time-averaged eddy-viscosity error; runtime was about 0.2 versus 330 core-hours for Nek5000.
watch_item: Coarse-mesh resolution still limits velocity accuracy, and generalization beyond the evaluated MSFR conditions remains unestablished.
paper_title: An Invariant Neural-Network Eddy-Viscosity Closure with Iterative Solver Coupling for Molten Salt Fast Reactor Thermal-Hydraulics
